Let other programs drive the 3D viewers

Source: R/remote_control.R
viewer_hub.Rd

A viewer can join a small hub that runs on this computer; R, Python or AI agents then send commands to the viewer through the hub and read back what it shows. These functions start, list and stop hubs. The hub is a Node.js program (version 18 or newer) that comes with this package; viewer_hub_path() gives its location.

Usage

viewer_hub_path()

viewer_hub_start(
  port = 17285L,
  key = NULL,
  generate_key = FALSE,
  idle_minutes = 30
)

viewer_hub_list(port = 17285L)

viewer_hub_stop(port = 17285L)

Arguments

port

the port of the hub; default is 17285

key

a key that the hub requires (letters, digits, "_" and "-"), or NULL for none

generate_key

whether the hub requires a random key; ignored when key is given

idle_minutes

the hub stops after this many minutes with nothing connected; 0 keeps it running

Value

viewer_hub_path(): the path of the hub script. viewer_hub_start(): the passkey, invisibly. viewer_hub_list(): a data frame of the running hubs, with columns port, passkey (NA when the key is unknown), keyed, viewers, by (who started it) and started. viewer_hub_stop(): nothing.

Details

viewer_hub_start() reuses the hub that already runs on port, or starts one in the background. It returns the hub's passkey: the port, or "port.key" when the hub requires a key, and stores it in options(threeBrain.remote_passkey), so viewers made afterwards show it in their "Passkey" field. To connect a viewer, click "Connect" below that field in its control panel; a viewer never connects by itself.

Without a key, any program or web page on this computer can connect to the hub; set generate_key = TRUE (or key) when that matters. The hub only listens on 127.0.0.1, so other computers cannot reach it.

Running hubs are recorded in tools::R_user_dir("threeBrain", "cache"), where other programs and AI agents find and join them. To let an agent drive the viewers, register the hub's MCP mode once, for example with Claude Code:

claude mcp add threebrain -- node /path/to/threebrain-hub.mjs mcp

where the path is viewer_hub_path(). The examples in the package repository (examples/WebSocket) show how R and Python scripts send commands.

The hub itself does not need R. Collaborators who received a viewer saved with save_brain run the same file through an agent plugin (examples/mcp in the package repository); their agent starts the hub and gives them the passkey.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{

passkey <- viewer_hub_start()

brain <- threeBrain(
  path = file.path(default_template_directory(), "N27"),
  subject_code = "N27", surface_types = "pial"
)
# In the viewer's control panel, click "Connect"
brain$plot()

viewer_hub_list()
viewer_hub_stop()
} # }
